title.value: Phenotypical predictors of pregnancy‐related restless legs syndrome and their association with basal ganglia and the limbic circuits
title.justification: The title reflects the primary focus of the study, which is to investigate predictors of pregnancy-related restless legs syndrome (RLS) and their connections with specific brain regions such as the basal ganglia and limbic circuits.
title.quote: Phenotypical predictors of pregnancy‐related restless legs syndrome and their association with basal ganglia and the limbic circuits

analysis.description: This study investigates the predictors of pregnancy-related restless legs syndrome (RLS) and their associations with brain structures, particularly the basal ganglia and limbic circuits. Using MRI data from postpartum women, the research employed a multivariate two-window algorithm to explore the relationship between brain morphology and phenotypical predictors of RLS.

type.justification: The study uses a neurological and obstetrical cohort of postpartum women and employs structural and functional MRI scans to investigate the relationship between phenotypic predictors and brain structures, indicating an empirical approach.
type.quote: A neurological and obstetrical cohort of 308 postpartum women was screened for RLS within 1 to 6 days of childbirth and 12 weeks postpartum. Structural and functional MRI was obtained from 25 of these 57 participants.

name.justification: The research primarily focuses on the investigation of brain structures related to restless legs syndrome during pregnancy, which falls under the study of Neuroscience, particularly due to the use of MRI scanning and analysis of brain morphology.
name.quote: A multivariate two-window algorithm was employed to systematically chart the relationship between brain structures and phenotypical predictors of RLS.

name.justification: The study utilizes structural and functional MRI scans to explore brain morphological patterns associated with RLS, which is a core aspect of Neuroimaging.
name.quote: Structural and functional MRI was obtained from 25 of these 57 participants.

name.justification: The study explores psychiatric aspects like depression and stress in relation to RLS, thus contributing to the field of Psychiatry.
name.quote: Participants with RLS symptoms during pregnancy were identified and compared with the rest of the sample. Additionally, a number of clinical and anamnestic indicators of RLS in pregnancy were assessed.

name.justification: The paper mentions the use of a multivariate pattern-learning algorithm, such as canonical correlation analysis (CCA), to analyze the relationship between brain structures and phenotypical predictors of RLS.
name.quote: An innovative multivariate pattern-learning algorithm (involving canonical correlation analysis or CCA) was employed to conjointly characterize patterns of brain structure and the phenotypical predictors of RLS, facilitating an objective assessment of their complex interplay.

is_contributed.justification: The paper contributes an innovative use of a multivariate pattern-learning algorithm to analyze the relationship between brain structure and phenotypical predictors of RLS.
is_contributed.quote: An innovative multivariate pattern-learning algorithm (involving canonical correlation analysis or CCA) was employed to conjointly characterize patterns of brain structure and the phenotypical predictors of RLS.

is_executed.justification: The multivariate pattern-learning algorithm was actively used to analyze the MRI data and phenotypical predictors in the study.
is_executed.quote: A single statistically significant CCA mode emerged in the first analysis (r = 0.993, p < 0.05), exhibiting a strong covariation of brain volume measures and diverse anamnestic and clinical indicators.

is_compared.justification: The model was not compared numerically to other models as the focus was on exploring relationships between phenotypical predictors and brain morphology.
is_compared.quote: An innovative multivariate pattern-learning algorithm (involving canonical correlation analysis or CCA) was employed.
